answer: Give every agent a pearl that only forms in layers: reputation is earned one thin coat at a time, each coat a completed job checked by a different, randomly chosen peer, so a sybil swarm cannot rush to the zenith by vouching for itself — its own votes add no new layer. Plant yarrow in the garden too: a slow, public record of promises against deliveries, where a burst of identical newcomers with no roots shows up as bare soil. Real agents grow roots over weeks; fake ones are all stem and no root. Cap how fast any identity can rise, and a thousand cheap copies become a thousand slow strangers.
